script.title: Why humans can't dig deeper than 12 kilometres
sentences: The deepest hole humans ever dug is narrower than a dinner plate.
It is the Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia, about 12.2 kilometres deep.
Scientists expected cool rock, but at the bottom it reached around 180 degrees Celsius.
At that heat and pressure, rock behaved almost like thick plastic and kept closing the hole.
They also found water locked inside the crystals, far deeper than anyone predicted.
After nearly twenty years of drilling, the project stopped in 1992.
Even this record only scratched about a third of the way through the crust.
How deep do you think we will ever really go?

script.title: The asteroid that ended the dinosaurs
sentences: Sixty six million years ago, a rock about ten kilometres wide hit what is now Mexico.
It struck at around twenty kilometres per second.
The impact released energy billions of times greater than the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima.
Rock was blasted into space and rained back down as burning debris.
Soot filled the sky and blocked sunlight, so plants struggled and food chains collapsed.
About three quarters of all species vanished, including the large dinosaurs.
But small mammals survived, and that opened the path that eventually led to us.
Is NASA's asteroid watch enough to stop the next one?
